For a domain codec, register a named `FieldSpec<T, E>` with `install_field_specs`, set `spec-key` and receive `committed(FieldCommit)`; `spec.accept(commit)` returns the validated domain value to Rust. `commit-policy` chooses blur, submit or each valid change. `ownership: Ownership.controlled` emits proposals and waits for `acknowledge(FieldValue)`. `field-state` and `accepted-text` expose the shared state; the native draft stays editable while incomplete. See the Forms guide for shared constraints and the Controllers guide for codecs. Native editing functions: `set-selection(anchor, cursor)` and `cursor-position`/`selection-anchor` use UTF-8 byte offsets; `insert-at-cursor(text)` focuses and inserts through the native input path, preserving undo and filters. `cut-selection()`, `paste()`, `undo()`, `redo()` and `blur()` forward native APIs. The localisable standard context menu honors access and password privacy; disable with `TextContextMenu.disabled`. Set `KitStrings` once per window to localise all default validation, codec, phone, action and counter messages; instance message properties remain overrides. Count labels support singular/plural; bounded length/range messages use `{count}`/`{value}` templates. For `FieldBinding`, pass `window.global::<KitStrings>().get_fields()` to `set_messages()`; domain error callbacks still supply their own translations. `show-character-count` works without host counting after `install()`: default `character-count` counts Unicode grapheme clusters. `CharacterCountFormat.of-max` and `.remaining` use UTF-16 units to match HTML `max-length`; templates live in `KitStrings`. Override `character-count-text` for a custom format and set `character-count-warning-threshold` for the theme warning color near the bound. Compose interactive content inside the same surface with KitInputGroupStart/End children; bind their layout-order to leading-adornment-order/trailing-adornment-order. Use focus-on-pointer: false on an auxiliary button that should keep native editing focus. Native Tab order follows declaration: editor, built-in actions, then custom children in their declaration order; visual layout-order does not reorder keyboard focus.
en.behavior: The example accepts nonempty text on blur or Accept. Native editing keeps caret, selection and undo. `text-cell-width` measures the zero glyph in the actual editor font; the OTP reads `theme.typography.family-monospace` for a predictable cell without approximating native metrics. `length-policy` defaults to `TextLengthPolicy.validate`: length constraints validate without rewriting native edits. Opt into `TextLengthPolicy.limit` for strict UTF-16 input limits, with the OTP overflow/history behavior described in its reference. On-change acceptance runs after the complete native edit, including synchronous host updates and length limits; navigation keys do not emit commits. Blur commits only changed drafts. HTML length constraints use the actual user-edit flag; validation timing also gates codec errors. Programmatic text corrections clear stale transition errors. `report-validity()` updates error visibility without moving focus. Call `focus-if-invalid()` explicitly for the first invalid field. `clear()` and the search clear action use a native delete transaction, preserve undo and dispatch the same edit/commit policy as typing. Reset, cancel and number-step assignments deliberately replace the editing baseline and reset native undo history. `key-pressed(KeyEvent) -> KitKeyResult` runs before filtering/native editing only when no IME preedit is active. `escape-behavior` defaults to clear for search and bubble otherwise; `.cancel` restores the accepted value and emits `cancelled()`. An empty search lets Escape bubble. Multiline fields can opt into Ctrl/Cmd+Enter submission using `submit-on-modified-enter`. Accessibility: the native editor exposes placeholder, help plus visible error, required text, prefix/suffix, counter and pending state; hidden passwords omit the value. The label shows localisable required text (`show-required-indicator` can hide it). Pending checks request a polite live announcement. Slint 1.18 lacks native accessible required/invalid states, email/URL/telephone keyboard content types and OTP autofill; descriptive text is the supported workaround. Headless tests do not qualify screen-reader, IME or device behavior. Public keyboard hooks return the shared KitKeyResult enum: KitKeyResult.accept consumes the key, .reject preserves built-in behavior. Rust uses slint_kit::ui::KitKeyResult::{Accept, Reject} without private Slint APIs. clearable applies to any single-line purpose, and reveal-toggle controls the independent password action. Clear and reveal can coexist. Built-in pointer actions preserve editor focus; their keyboard activation restores it. busy is independent of validation and keeps both pending labels when needed. A host that requires a read-only busy value must set access explicitly. The surface’s intrinsic height follows the tallest adornment while the native viewport keeps its intrinsic minimum and fills the available row. Text defaults use logical start alignment for labels, legends, help, errors, placeholders, formatted text and the native editor. The kit projects logical Start/End to physical Left/Right using theme.direction; it does not infer direction from paragraph contents. Native Slint 1.18.1 Software Start was observed at Left, so this explicit kit mapping also covers labels/help/errors, placeholders and formatted text. Set theme.direction once using the shared ChoiceFlow enum; flow defaults to that direction and overrides only the visual row for one field. The complete built-in surface row mirrors, including icons, prefix/suffix, busy, clear and reveal; Start/End parts follow their projected layout-order. Native Tab remains declaration order. Native focus loss can collapse a selected range; keyboard clear/reveal actions restore editor focus, while pointer actions keep focus and selection. Layout inside custom parts remains the caller’s responsibility. OTP keeps an explicit left text default.
en.label: Text Field

text.effect: The native editing draft, bound two-way to the editor's `TextInput`: it changes on every keystroke, paste and IME commit and may hold an incomplete value. The accepted value lives in `field-state.accepted` and `accepted-text`, so read `text` for the draft and `committed(FieldCommit)` for the value.
text.states: Read-only keeps native selection, caret and copy but refuses edits; disabled refuses focus. While the field has no focus and a codec formats the accepted value, the formatted projection (`display-text`) is painted over the unchanged draft.
text.constraints: With `length-policy: TextLengthPolicy.limit` and `max-length >= 0`, text beyond the limit (UTF-16 code units) is removed from the native edit once `slint_kit::install` has run.

label.effect: Shows a `KitFieldLabel` above the editor when nonempty; clicking it focuses the editor. It is also the accessible name of the editor unless `accessible-name` overrides it.
label.default: `""`: no label row is rendered, so set `accessible-name` to keep the editor named.
label.states: The label follows `access`: dimmed when disabled, unchanged when read-only.

description.effect: Help text included in the native editor accessible description alongside validation messages. show-description (true by default) controls only its visible helper row.

error.effect: A message decided by the application, shown as a `KitFieldError` under the editor when `validation` is `ValidationPresentation.invalid`. It enters the shared constraint engine as a custom validity, so `validity.custom-error` is set and `validation-message` repeats it.
error.states: Ignored while `validation` is not `invalid`. A failing HTML constraint, a codec error reported in `field-state.error` or a nonempty `custom-validity` takes precedence over it. `show-validation-message: false` hides the row and keeps the invalid presentation.

placeholder.effect: Hint painted inside the editor while `text` is empty and no IME composition is in progress; it follows `text-alignment` and the editor font. It is never the accessible name: use `label` or `accessible-name` for that.

access.effect: Who may change the value: `editable`, `read-only` or `disabled`. It drives the editor, the label, the surface recipe and the constraint engine at once.
access.states: `read-only`: native selection, caret and copy stay; edits, commits and `step-number` are refused; the surface takes the canvas tone and `will-validate` becomes false, as with HTML `readonly`. `disabled`: the editor refuses focus and pointer, label and text are dimmed, `accessible-enabled` is false and nothing validates.

required.effect: Declares the value mandatory for the shared HTML constraint engine: an empty value sets `validity.value-missing` and `validation-message` becomes `required-message`.
required.states: Shown according to `validation-timing` or after `report-validity()`; not evaluated while the field is read-only or disabled.

min-length.effect: Minimum length of the value for the constraint engine, counted in UTF-16 code units like HTML `minlength`; a shorter nonempty value sets `validity.too-short` with `too-short-message`.
min-length.constraints: Applies to the text input kinds, as in HTML; numbers and dates ignore it.

max-length.effect: Maximum length of the value in UTF-16 code units, like HTML `maxlength`. Under `length-policy: TextLengthPolicy.validate` a longer value only sets `validity.too-long` with `too-long-message`; under `TextLengthPolicy.limit` the native edit is cut at the limit.

length-policy.effect: How `max-length` is enforced. `validate` reports `too-long` and leaves the native edit, undo history and IME composition alone; `limit` removes the overflow from the editor through its public undo, text and selection APIs, which can discard the native undo entry of the rejected edit.
length-policy.constraints: `limit` needs the shared engine installed by `slint_kit::install`; until it is ready the editor stays read-only so no unbounded text slips through. `KitOtpField` uses `limit`.

pattern.effect: A regular expression the whole value must match, with HTML `pattern` semantics (ECMAScript `v` syntax, anchored to the full value); a mismatch sets `validity.pattern-mismatch` with `pattern-message`. `pattern-enabled` defaults to `pattern != ""`.
pattern.constraints: Compiled by the shared engine; a pattern that does not compile is reported in `pattern-error`. Not applied to a multiline field, as HTML does not apply it to a text area. With `purpose: email` and `multiple`, every address must match.

min.effect: Lower bound of a numeric, date or time value, written as text in the canonical form of the input kind (for example `"0"` or `"2026-01-01"`); a smaller value sets `validity.range-underflow` with `underflow-message`. It is also the base of the `step` check and of `step-number`.
min.constraints: Read by the HTML engine for the number, date, month, week, time and date-time kinds; text kinds ignore it. The parser of a `FieldSpec` keeps its own domain bounds.

max.effect: Upper bound of a numeric, date or time value, as text in the canonical form of the input kind; a larger value sets `validity.range-overflow` with `overflow-message`. A time range with `max` before `min` crosses midnight, as in HTML.

step.effect: Granularity of a numeric, date or time value, as text: a value that is not the base (`min`, else `default-value`, else zero) plus a whole number of steps sets `validity.step-mismatch` with `step-message`; `"any"` disables the check. `step-number(direction)` and the buttons of `KitNumberStepper` move the draft by one step and never leave `[min, max]`.
step.default: `""`: the default step of the kind, 1 for numbers. `KitIntegerField` sets `"1"`; `KitDecimalField` and its variants set `"any"`.

default-value.effect: The value `reset-field()` restores as draft and accepted value, with a cleared validation state. It is also the base of the `step` check when `min` is empty, as the HTML `value` attribute is. It does not initialize `text`.

commit-policy.effect: When an acceptable draft becomes the accepted value and `committed(FieldCommit)` fires: `on-blur` when the editor loses focus or on Enter, `on-submit` only on Enter or `commit()`, `on-change-when-valid` on each edit that passes the constraints and the codec.
commit-policy.states: A draft the constraints or the codec reject is never committed: `field-state.error` carries the message and `invalid()` fires. `cancel-edit()` restores the last accepted draft.

ownership.effect: Who owns the accepted value. `local`: the field accepts the draft itself and `committed` reports the new value. `controlled`: `committed` is a proposal; the accepted value stays as it was until the host calls `acknowledge(FieldValue)`.

spec-key.effect: Names a `FieldSpec<T, E>` installed in Rust with `install_field_specs`. The codec validates the draft at commit time (its message lands in `field-state.error`), formats the accepted value at rest (`display-text`) and travels in `FieldCommit.spec`, so `spec.accept(commit)` refuses a commit meant for another field.
spec-key.default: `""`: plain text with the HTML constraints only.
spec-key.constraints: The key is application data, independent of the field's position; `FieldSpecKey::new` rejects an empty key. Call `slint_kit::install` and `install_field_specs` before the window shows.

field-state.effect: The shared field state: `accepted` (presence and text of the accepted value), `draft`, `dirty` and `touched`, `error` of the last refused commit, `committed` for the last transition and `value`, the candidate of that transition.
field-state.default: Initialized from `text` at creation: accepted value and draft both equal the initial text.
field-state.states: Updated by the edit, blur, submit and cancel actions while the field is editable; `acknowledge(FieldValue)` replaces `accepted` under `Ownership.controlled`; `reset-field()` restores `default-value`.

accepted-text.effect: The text of the last accepted value, `field-state.accepted.text`, as a plain string for bindings; it does not change while the user edits the draft.
accepted-text.example:
name := KitTextField { label: "Name"; text: "Ada"; }
Text { text: "Saved: " + name.accepted-text; }

validation.effect: The presentation the application asks for: `pristine`, `checking` (a spinner in the surface and `checking-label` under the editor, for an asynchronous check), `valid`, or `invalid` (danger border and focus ring, `error` shown).
validation.states: A failing HTML constraint or a codec error forces the invalid presentation whatever this value is. `valid` has no distinct rendering in the shipped field recipe.

validation-timing.effect: When a failing HTML constraint becomes visible without `report-validity()`: `on-blur` once the field was left (`touched`), `on-input` as soon as it was edited (`dirty`), `on-submit` only after `report-validity()`. A definitive error, such as an impossible email character, shows as soon as the field is dirty.

custom-validity.effect: A message that makes the value invalid until it is cleared, like `setCustomValidity`: `validity.custom-error` is set and `validation-message` repeats it. `set-custom-validity(message)` writes it; it takes precedence over the intrinsic error and over `error`.

validity.effect: HTML-style validity flags of the current value: `valid`, `value-missing`, `type-mismatch`, `pattern-mismatch`, `too-long`, `too-short`, `range-underflow`, `range-overflow`, `step-mismatch`, `bad-input` and `custom-error`, computed by the shared engine from the constraints and `validation-text`.
validity.states: Not evaluated while `will-validate` is false (read-only or disabled); `validation-ready` reports whether the shared engine is installed.
validity.example:
email := KitEmailField { label: "Email"; required: true; }
Text { text: email.validity.value-missing ? "Required" : ""; }

validation-message.effect: The message of the first failing constraint, in the order custom, required, type, pattern, too short, too long, underflow, overflow, step, bad input, taken from the matching `*-message` property; `""` while the value is valid or not validated. The built-in `KitFieldError` row shows it when `show-validation-message` is true.
validation-message.example:
code := KitTextField { label: "Code"; pattern: "[0-9]{6}"; }
Text { text: code.validation-message; }

show-validation-message.effect: Whether the built-in `KitFieldError` row renders under the editor. Off, the invalid presentation and the accessible description are kept and the host shows the message elsewhere, as `KitDataTable` does for its cell editor and `KitNumberStepper` for its own row.

purpose.effect: The semantic purpose of the text. It selects the HTML constraint kind through `input-kind` (`email`, `url`, `telephone`, `password`, `search`), the native masking of a password and its reveal button, the clear button of a search, the input-method hints (`plain` gets sentence capitalization, auto-correct and auto-complete; the others none) and the default leading search icon.
purpose.constraints: `email` and `url` do not accept arbitrary nonempty text: the shared engine checks the address or absolute-URL syntax, and `email-message` or `url-message` carries the message.

input-type.effect: Declares the editor input behavior. `decimal` sets `input-kind` to `number`; after `install`, the shared numeric filter admits incomplete exponents and configured localized drafts while the native editor uses `InputType.text`. `password` masks the text. See the [numeric platform limits](../../guides/forms/): this does not preserve the native editor’s `NumberInput` role or request a numeric soft keyboard independently.
input-type.constraints: Filtering shapes the draft only; parsing, bounds and exact arithmetic stay with the HTML engine and the `FieldSpec`.

control-size.effect: Height, padding, icon size and font size of the surface, from the theme's density metrics; shared by every control of the kit so a row of fields and buttons stays aligned.

decoration.effect: The surface the `KitInputGroup` draws around the editor: `boxed` draws the bordered box of the field recipe; `underlined` draws only a bottom line, split into `underline-segments` parts (`KitOtpField` uses one per slot). `cells` draws one themed box per underline-segments with optional group-size markers; the same single native editor remains above it.

prefix.effect: Secondary text inside the surface, before the editor, in the editor font and the secondary tone. It is neither part of `text` nor of the validated value; use `leading-icon` for a glyph.

suffix.effect: Secondary text inside the surface, after the editor, in the editor font and the secondary tone; neither part of `text` nor of the value. `KitPercentField` sets `"%"`; a duration field names its unit here, matching the explicit DurationUnit of its Rust codec; this text performs no conversion.

line-mode.effect: `single-line` keeps one line, commits on Enter and scrolls horizontally. `multiline` wraps words, lets Enter insert a line break instead of committing, scrolls vertically and sizes the editor from `min-lines`, `max-lines` and `resize-policy`. `KitTextArea` sets `multiline`.
line-mode.constraints: A multiline field validates as an HTML text area: `pattern` is not applied, and the reveal and clear buttons are not shown.

resize-policy.effect: How a multiline editor takes its height: `fixed` shows `min-lines` lines and scrolls inside; `auto-grow` grows with the text up to `max-lines`, then scrolls. `KitTextArea` sets `auto-grow`.

min-lines.effect: Lines a multiline editor always shows (at least one line is kept).

max-lines.effect: Lines a multiline editor grows to under `ResizePolicy.auto-grow` before it scrolls; never fewer than `min-lines`.

clearable.effect: Show a native clear action for a nonempty single-line field of any purpose. Read-only, disabled and active composition refuse clearing. Escape behavior remains a separate policy.

reveal-toggle.effect: Show or hide the password reveal button with SecretToggleVisibility. This controls the affordance; secret-visibility still controls the actual value presentation. Read-only passwords remain selectable and may be revealed; disabled controls and composition refuse the action.

busy.effect: Display an indeterminate activity mark and a polite status independently of validation. Editing and custom action availability remain governed by FieldAccess and their own guards. When validation is checking too, both status labels remain in the accessible description.
busy.example: KitTextField { label: "Project"; busy: true; busy-label: "Loading project…"; }

busy-label.effect: Localizable visible and accessible activity status. Set KitStrings.busy-label once per window or override this instance.

leading-adornment-order.effect: Read-only native layout order for a leading composition part. Bind the child part’s layout-order to this value; no editor or commit logic is rebuilt. Its sign changes with flow; bind the projection instead of a fixed integer.

trailing-adornment-order.effect: Read-only native layout order for a trailing composition part. Custom actions retain their own accessible names and availability. Its sign changes with flow; bind the projection instead of a fixed integer.

page-steps.effect: Number of steps PageUp and PageDown move a number field, as a whole number. Up/Down move one step; Home/End jump to `min`/`max` when that bound is set and otherwise keep their native caret movement. Keys step only while `step` is not `"any"` and `access` is editable; every step goes through the exact HTML step engine, replaces the draft like typed text (`edited`, `value-edited`, dirty, native undo) and follows `commit-policy`. A step clamped at a bound edits nothing.
page-steps.constraints: A count below one steps nothing. Modified arrows (Control, Meta, Alt) are left to the native editor, and a `key-pressed` hook that returns `accept` runs first.

wheel-stepping.effect: Whether the mouse wheel steps a focused number field: wheel up increments, wheel down decrements, by one step each, through the same step path as the arrow keys. An unfocused field leaves the wheel to its scroll view.

flow.effect: Mirrors the built-in adornment row and the Start/End placement using the existing ChoiceFlow. It leaves the native editor, text offsets, logical payload and declaration-order Tab unchanged.

text-alignment.effect: Native editor, placeholder and formatted display alignment. Start/End resolve to physical Left/Right from theme.direction, independently of paragraph contents; explicit left/center/right pass through unchanged. The flow override changes only adornment order.

validation-mask.effect: Mask prefix guard for a custom composition. Use KitMaskedField to also derive length bounds, pattern, placeholder and configuration errors; this lower-level hook filters ordinary ASCII typing and explicit paste without rewriting text.
validation-mask.states: A nonempty mask requires installed validation; native deletes and non-keyboard text remain subject to full-draft HTML validation.
validation-mask.constraints: Use the declared #/A/*/escaped-literal grammar. This property does not derive the other constraints.

constraints.effect: Read-only shared HTML constraints for the current native draft. Carry this exact projection in FieldCommit to FieldSpec::accept at the Rust submission boundary.

implicit-form-submit.effect: Participates in the enclosing KitForm’s native Enter protocol. Set false on auxiliary editors whose Enter action belongs to their own widget.

error-visible.effect: Read-only shared constraint visibility, inherited by text-based fields. Manual domain error presentation remains observable through validation-visible.

edit-filter.effect: Typed insertion policy: unfiltered (default) or a complete-draft HTML pattern accepting valid prefixes. The shared HTML engine caches its compiled rule. Ordinary key/explicit-paste checks preserve native selection and undo; bypassed IME/backend paths remain validated after insertion without an invented editor model.

edit-filter-message.effect: Localized configuration error for an invalid edit filter, from KitStrings.text-filter-message.

edit-filter-error.effect: Read-only diagnostic; nonempty errors block acceptance through the shared constraint engine.

completion-policy.effect: manual by default; at-max-length emits completed after a native edit reaches a positive max-length and all shared constraints pass. Host assignments do not emit.

group-size.effect: Decorative cell grouping interval for FieldDecoration.cells; zero disables group markers. It never inserts a separator into text or changes native selection offsets.

show-description.effect: show-description:false hides only the visual helper; description still reaches the native editor. This lets a composed field render its help once outside the editor.

modal-layer.effect: The modal layer this control belongs to; 0 is the window. While a `KitDialogSurface` or `KitDrawer` with a positive `modal-layer` is open and topmost, every kit control whose `modal-layer` differs is inert: it takes no focus, ignores pointer and keys, and reports itself disabled to assistive technology. Give a control placed inside a modal that modal's layer number.

theme.effect: The `KitTheme` the field reads its colors, radius, spacing, typography and focus ring from. Every kit control follows the window theme by default; bind this property to give one field another theme.

input-kind.effect: The HTML input type the shared constraint engine validates against: `email` and `url` check the syntax, `number` the range and step, `telephone` the structure. Derived from `purpose`, `input-type` and `multiline`, so the built-in fields set it for you; override it only for a custom skin.
input-kind.default: Derived: `HtmlInputKind.text-area` when multiline, `number` for `InputType.decimal`, otherwise the kind that matches `purpose`, else `text`.

number-range.effect: Read-only `minimum`, `maximum` and `step` of a number field, parsed once from `min`, `max` and `step` and exposed to assistive technology as the accessible range. Other input kinds report no bounds (all zero).

number-format.effect: How a number field reads and writes the decimal separator: `canonical` accepts `.` only, `decimal-comma` accepts a comma as in French. It changes parsing and validation of the typed text, not the accepted value, which stays canonical.

validation-text.effect: The text the constraints are checked against. It follows `text`; a custom skin binds it to a normalized form of the draft (the telephone field strips separators) so the native draft stays untouched while validation sees the clean value.

display-text.effect: The text painted while the field has no focus and a codec formats the accepted value (for example a money amount with its currency). The draft in `text` is unchanged and returns as soon as the editor takes focus.
display-text.default: The codec projection registered under `spec-key` once the draft is accepted; otherwise `text`.

intrinsic-error.effect: A message a custom skin or codec wrapper sets when the typed text cannot be read as its type (the telephone, date and number fields use it). While nonempty the value is invalid and `validation-message` shows it, below `custom-validity` in priority.

show-required-indicator.effect: Whether the label shows the required marker when `required` is true. Set it to false when every field of the form is required and the marker only adds noise; `required` still validates and still reaches the accessible description.

required-label.effect: Text of the required marker next to the label and in the accessible description. Localise it once with `KitStrings`, or set it on one field.

multiple.effect: For `KitEmailField`, accepts a comma-separated list of addresses and checks each one, like the HTML `multiple` attribute. Other input kinds ignore it.

pattern-enabled.effect: Whether `pattern` takes part in validation. It follows `pattern`, so a nonempty pattern is checked and an empty one is not; bind it to false to keep the pattern declared but suspended.

required-message.effect: Message of `validity.value-missing` when a `required` field is empty. It becomes `validation-message` if it is the first failing constraint. Set it on one field, or localise the default for the window with `KitStrings`.

email-message.effect: Message of `validity.type-mismatch` when the text is not a valid email address. It becomes `validation-message` if it is the first failing constraint. Set it on one field, or localise the default for the window with `KitStrings`.

url-message.effect: Message of `validity.type-mismatch` when the text is not a valid absolute URL. It becomes `validation-message` if it is the first failing constraint. Set it on one field, or localise the default for the window with `KitStrings`.

pattern-message.effect: Message of `validity.pattern-mismatch` when the text does not match `pattern`. It becomes `validation-message` if it is the first failing constraint. Set it on one field, or localise the default for the window with `KitStrings`.

too-short-message.effect: Message of `validity.too-short` when the edited text is shorter than `min-length`. It becomes `validation-message` if it is the first failing constraint. Set it on one field, or localise the default for the window with `KitStrings`.

too-long-message.effect: Message of `validity.too-long` when the text is longer than `max-length` under `TextLengthPolicy.validate`. It becomes `validation-message` if it is the first failing constraint. Set it on one field, or localise the default for the window with `KitStrings`.

underflow-message.effect: Message of `validity.range-underflow` when a number is below `min`. It becomes `validation-message` if it is the first failing constraint. Set it on one field, or localise the default for the window with `KitStrings`.

overflow-message.effect: Message of `validity.range-overflow` when a number is above `max`. It becomes `validation-message` if it is the first failing constraint. Set it on one field, or localise the default for the window with `KitStrings`.

step-message.effect: Message of `validity.step-mismatch` when a number is not a multiple of `step` from `min`. It becomes `validation-message` if it is the first failing constraint. Set it on one field, or localise the default for the window with `KitStrings`.

bad-input-message.effect: Message of `validity.bad-input` when the text cannot be read as the field type, for example letters in a number field. It becomes `validation-message` if it is the first failing constraint. Set it on one field, or localise the default for the window with `KitStrings`.

will-validate.effect: Read-only: whether constraints apply now. It is false while the field is disabled or read-only, like an HTML control that is barred from constraint validation, and true otherwise. `validity` and `report-validity()` check it.

validation-ready.effect: Read-only: whether the shared constraint engine is installed for the window. It becomes true after `slint_kit::install(&app)`; before that, `validity` reports no failure rather than guessing.

pattern-error.effect: Read-only: the compile error of `pattern` when the expression is invalid, `""` when it compiles or is empty. An invalid pattern is a developer mistake and is reported here instead of rejecting every value.

value.effect: Read-only: the semantic value after the shared engine normalizes the draft, for example without separators for a telephone number. Prefer `committed(FieldCommit)` for the accepted value; `value` follows each keystroke like `edited`.

dirty.effect: Read-only: true once the user has edited the text, like the HTML dirty value flag. Programmatic changes do not set it; `reset-validation()` and `reset-field()` clear it. `on-input` validation timing and the length constraints read it.

touched.effect: Read-only: true once the field has been focused and left. `validation-timing: ValidationTiming.on-blur` shows constraint errors only after it; `reset-validation()` clears it.

secret-visibility.effect: Whether a password field shows its text. `hidden` masks it; `revealed` shows it. The reveal button toggles it and `secret-visibility-changed` reports the change; bind it two-way to keep several fields in step. Other purposes ignore it.

accessible-name.effect: Name announced for the editor by assistive technology. It follows `label`; set it when the field has no visible label, such as a search box in a toolbar.

input-method-hints.effect: Capitalization, autocorrect and autocomplete requests sent to the platform keyboard or IME, within what Slint exposes. Built-in purposes already choose sensible values; set it for text such as a username where autocorrect is unwanted.
input-method-hints.default: Plain text: sentence capitalization with autocorrect and autocomplete; every other purpose: none.

validation-visible.effect: Read-only: whether the field presents itself as invalid, from a failing constraint, a manual `validation: ValidationPresentation.invalid` or a codec error. Use it to style surrounding content; it differs from `validity`, which ignores timing.

underline-segments.effect: Number of cells drawn for `decoration: FieldDecoration.underlined` or `cells`; one draws a single line. `KitOtpField` sets it to its slot count. A value below one counts as one.

text-font-family.effect: Font family of the editor, the formatted text and the placeholder. Cell-based fields set the monospace family so each character has the same width.

text-inset.effect: Horizontal offset of the text from the start edge of the editor, used to center a character in a cell. It shifts the caret, selection and context menu with the text.

text-cell-width.effect: Read-only: the width of the zero glyph in the actual editor font and size. Cell layouts divide it into the cell width so each character sits at the center of its cell without approximating native metrics.

text-letter-spacing.effect: Extra space added after each character. Cell layouts use it to spread characters across their cells; leave it at zero for ordinary text.

leading-icon.effect: Theme glyph drawn before the text, on the reading-start side. A search field shows the search icon by default; an empty glyph draws nothing. Icons are decorative, so keep the meaning in `label` or `accessible-name`.
leading-icon.default: The search icon for `TextPurpose.search`; otherwise no icon.

trailing-icon.effect: Theme glyph drawn after the text, on the reading-end side. It is decorative; interactive actions such as clear and reveal are separate buttons.

corner-radius.effect: Corner radius of the field surface. It defaults to the radius of the control recipe, so it follows the theme and `control-size`; override it only to match a surrounding composition.

padding-inline.effect: Space between the field edge and its content on the inline axis. It defaults to the control recipe, so it scales with `control-size` and `text-scale`.

padding-block.effect: Space between the field edge and its content on the block axis. It defaults to the control recipe; the height still grows with `text-scale`.

text-size.effect: Font size of the editor text. It defaults to the control recipe, which already multiplies by the theme `text-scale`; an explicit value replaces that scaling.

show-character-count.effect: Shows a counter row under the editor and adds it to the accessible description. After `slint_kit::install` it counts Unicode grapheme clusters; the limit of `max-length` is still measured in UTF-16 code units.

character-count.effect: The number shown by the counter. It counts the grapheme clusters of `text`; bind it only to count another way, such as words.
character-count.default: Grapheme count of `text`, 0 until `slint_kit::install` has run.

character-count-format.effect: Shape of the counter text: `count` shows the number and the unit (`12 characters`), `of-max` shows `used / max`, `remaining` shows what is left. Without a nonnegative `max-length`, `of-max` and `remaining` fall back to `count`.

character-count-warning-threshold.effect: How many characters before `max-length` the counter enters its warning state. Zero warns only at the limit; a negative value counts as zero. It does not block input.

character-count-warning.effect: Read-only: true when the used length (UTF-16 code units) is within `character-count-warning-threshold` of `max-length` or beyond it, and false without a nonnegative `max-length`. Bind host styling to it.

character-count-text.effect: The counter string as displayed and announced. It is composed from `character-count-format` and the localised templates; bind it only to replace the whole text.

reveal-label.effect: Accessible name and tooltip text of the button that reveals the password. Localise it once for the window with `KitStrings`, or set it on one field.

hide-label.effect: Accessible name and tooltip text of the button that hides the password again. Localise it once for the window with `KitStrings`, or set it on one field.

clear-label.effect: Accessible name of the clear button, shown when `clearable` is true. Search fields use their own default wording. Localise it once for the window with `KitStrings`, or set it on one field.

character-count-label.effect: Unit word of the `count` counter format, with the singular form for exactly one character. Localise it once for the window with `KitStrings`, or set it on one field.

checking-label.effect: Text announced while `validation` is `ValidationPresentation.checking`, for example during a server uniqueness check. Localise it once for the window with `KitStrings`, or set it on one field.

undo-label.effect: Text of the Undo item of the context menu. Localise it once for the window with `KitStrings`, or set it on one field.

redo-label.effect: Text of the Redo item of the context menu. Localise it once for the window with `KitStrings`, or set it on one field.

cut-label.effect: Text of the Cut item of the context menu. Localise it once for the window with `KitStrings`, or set it on one field.

copy-label.effect: Text of the Copy item of the context menu. Localise it once for the window with `KitStrings`, or set it on one field.

paste-label.effect: Text of the Paste item of the context menu. Localise it once for the window with `KitStrings`, or set it on one field.

select-all-label.effect: Text of the Select all item of the context menu. Localise it once for the window with `KitStrings`, or set it on one field.

has-focus.effect: Read-only: true while the native editor or its owned context menu has focus. Opening the context menu keeps it true, so styling does not flicker. Other buttons of the field are separate focus targets.

escape-behavior.effect: What Escape does inside the editor: `bubble` leaves it to the parent (a dialog closes), `cancel` restores the accepted text through `cancel-edit()` and emits `cancelled`, `clear` empties a nonempty editable field. Read-only and disabled fields never edit.

submit-on-modified-enter.effect: For a multiline editor, makes Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter validate and commit while plain Enter keeps inserting a newline. It emits `commit-requested`. Single-line fields always commit on Enter, so this has no effect on them.

cursor-position.effect: Read-only: the caret as a UTF-8 byte offset into `text`. Pass it, not a character index, to `set-selection(anchor, cursor)`; it equals `selection-anchor` when nothing is selected.

selection-anchor.effect: Read-only: the fixed end of the selection as a UTF-8 byte offset into `text`. The selected range lies between `selection-anchor` and `cursor-position`, whichever is smaller first.

context-menu.effect: Whether a right-click or the context-menu key opens the standard editing menu (undo, redo, cut, copy, paste, select all). `disabled` removes it. Items honor `access`, and a hidden password never offers copy or cut.

validation-twelve-hour.effect: For time-based custom skins, makes the engine read and validate times in 12-hour form with an AM/PM marker instead of 24-hour. The text fields themselves do not use it.

callbacks.edited: Final native draft after an accepted edit; reset-field() also notifies this callback. Rejected strict edits do not notify it.
callbacks.value-edited: Sanitized semantic value for the same native edit, distinct from the raw draft.
callbacks.committed: Accepted FieldCommit according to commit-policy, with value, shared constraints and codec key. Guard Rust commands with FieldSpec::accept.
callbacks.commit-requested: Single-line Enter or opted-in modified-Enter notification. Use committed for accepted payloads and retain the Rust codec guard.
callbacks.invalid: A requested validity check or explicit acceptance failed. Observing it does not replace checking the submitted value in Rust.
callbacks.focus-observed: Observes focus of the native editor or its owned editing menu; opening that menu does not commit a blur. Other action buttons are separate.
callbacks.cancelled: Emitted by cancel-edit() and the configured Escape cancellation policy.
callbacks.key-pressed: Runs before filtering/native editing only without active IME preedit. Return reject to retain native behavior or accept for a handled shortcut. Return KitKeyResult.accept or KitKeyResult.reject.
callbacks.cleared: Emitted after a nonempty clear action or clear() successfully empties the native editor, after ordinary edit/commit callbacks. An empty or refused clear emits nothing; undo remains native.
callbacks.secret-visibility-changed: Observe a real SecretVisibility transition, whether caused by the built-in reveal button or a host property update. This observation does not replace the native action guard.
callbacks.completed: A complete valid draft from a native edit, deduplicated until the complete value changes or becomes incomplete. It does not accept or submit; never log the code or expose it in status text.

functions.take-focus: Close the owned editing menu and focus the native editor unless disabled.
functions.blur: Close the owned editing menu and release the native editor’s focus.
functions.select-all: Select all text in the existing native editor.
functions.copy-selection: Forward native copy unless the password is hidden; read-only controls retain copying.
functions.cut-selection: Forward native cut only while editable and the password is not hidden.
functions.paste: Forward native paste only while editable and the same phone/numeric insertion checks as keyboard paste accept it.
functions.undo: Undo a native edit while editable. Slint may represent a replacement as separate deletion/insertion history entries.
functions.redo: Redo a native edit while editable.
functions.set-selection: Select between UTF-8 byte offsets (anchor, cursor); equal offsets place the caret without selecting.
functions.insert-at-cursor: Focus and insert through the native editing path, preserving the same editor and its history.
functions.clear: Delete all text through an undoable native edit and the ordinary edit/acceptance policy.
functions.commit: Report validity and request acceptance according to the shared field reducer; observe committed for an accepted payload.
functions.cancel-edit: Restore the accepted draft when editable and installed, then emit cancelled. This replaces the native editing baseline.
functions.acknowledge: Acknowledge the host’s accepted FieldValue without rewriting an active draft.
functions.reset-field: Restore default-value and accepted state, reset validation and notify edited. This replaces native undo history.
functions.step-number: Pointer stepping used by the `KitNumberStepper` buttons: rewrite the draft by one step and commit at once, without needing editor focus. Keyboard, wheel and accessible stepping use `step-by` instead.
functions.check-validity: Check constraints without changing reporting visibility; failure emits invalid.
functions.report-validity: Reveal constraint errors and return validity without moving focus.
functions.focus-if-invalid: Focus this field only if it participates in validation and is invalid; returns whether it requested focus.
functions.set-custom-validity: Set an application constraint message; an empty string clears that error.
functions.reset-validation: Clear HTML dirty/touched/reported presentation while retaining the current draft and accepted value.
functions.step-by: Step a number field by `count` steps in a direction through the native edit path, like Up/Down and PageUp/PageDown; returns whether stepping applied (also when clamped at a bound), false for text kinds, `step: "any"`, read-only or disabled fields.
functions.step-to-bound: Jump a number field to `min` (decrement) or `max` (increment) through the native edit path, like Home/End; returns false when that bound is absent.
functions.replace-draft: `replace-draft(string) -> bool`: focus the existing native editor, select the whole draft and request native replacement, retaining undo and normal edited/value-edited notifications. Returns false while disabled, read-only, in native preedit or without installed services. Replacement is an edit, not acceptance; commit-policy and shared constraints still decide acceptance.

en.accessibility: show-description:false hides only the visual helper; description still reaches the native editor. This lets a composed field render its help once outside the editor.
en.states: Editable fields preserve selection, caret, undo and IME. Read-only fields remain selectable and copyable; disabled fields reject editing and actions. Validation can be pristine, checking, valid or invalid; `validation-timing` controls HTML/codec error visibility, while explicit reporting reveals errors immediately. `validation-visible` observes that presentation. Password reveal retains the editor and changes `secret-visibility`; `input-method-hints` controls capitalization, autocorrect and autocomplete within Slint’s available input APIs. Optional clear, reveal and custom adornment actions keep their own disabled states; busy and validation checking may coexist.

fr.summary: Saisie native d’une heure locale.
fr.usage: `accepted-time: LocalTimeValue` est une valeur typée en entrée-sortie. `{}` ou `{present: false}` signifie absence ; `{present: true, time: {}}` représente minuit. Remplacez les anciennes affectations directes de `LocalTimeView` par `{present: true, time: value}`. Ne lisez `.time` que si `.present` vaut true. En propriété Local, une validation écrit la valeur typée analysée dans cette propriété (liaison bidirectionnelle `<=>` pour la partager) ; en Controlled, l’hôte l’acquitte. La propriété Local/Controlled gouverne aussi le FieldState partagé et `committed(FieldCommit)`. Protégez l’acceptation Rust avec le FieldSpec correspondant et conservez son résultat analysé. Importez le composant depuis `@kit`, définissez libellés et contraintes, puis appelez `slint_kit::install(&app)` une fois avant d’afficher la fenêtre. Le champ possède son brouillon natif `text` et sa valeur acceptée. Pour un codec métier, enregistrez un `FieldSpec<T, E>` nommé avec `install_field_specs`, définissez `spec-key` et recevez `committed(FieldCommit)` ; `spec.accept(commit)` retourne la valeur métier validée à Rust. `commit-policy` choisit la perte de focus, la soumission ou chaque changement valide. `ownership: Ownership.controlled` émet des propositions et attend `acknowledge(FieldValue)`. `field-state` et `accepted-text` exposent l’état partagé ; le brouillon natif reste modifiable lorsqu’il est incomplet. Les guides Formulaires et Contrôleurs détaillent contraintes partagées et codecs. L’heure typée doit respecter `precision` ; la précision à la minute refuse une seconde non nulle au lieu de la tronquer. `clock-format` gouverne le formatage sur 12/24 heures.
fr.behavior: Après `slint_kit::install(&window)`, un instantané hôte typé valide initialise la valeur acceptée de référence et formate le texte au repos, y compris pour un champ monté après installation. Les mises à jour hôte et l’absence explicite actualisent ensuite texte au repos et référence. Un brouillon initial explicitement défini, même vide, est conservé. Pendant le focus de l’éditeur natif, les mises à jour hôte acquittent la référence sans remplacer texte, curseur, sélection ni historique d’annulation ; la réconciliation intervient à la perte de focus ou à l’annulation. Les modèles typés invalides sont ignorés et ne représentent jamais une absence. La prévisualisation Slint seule nécessite un texte explicite ; la synchronisation typée exige les services Rust installés. Les preuves headless ne qualifient ni IME natif ni lecteur d’écran. LocalTime ne contient ni date ni fuseau horaire. Le libellé visible ne change pas le clock-format explicite. Les aperçus Slint seuls affichent le texte déclaré ; formatage typé, analyse et acceptation nécessitent les services Rust installés par `install(&window)`. Le guide de l’éditeur détaille les limites des aperçus. Flèche haut/bas modifie l’unité affichée la plus fine (minutes, ou secondes avec `precision: TimePrecision.second`) et Page précédente/suivante modifie les heures, dans les limites de `min`, `max` et `step`. Un brouillon qui n’est pas une heure reste à l’éditeur natif.
fr.label: Champ heure

Remplacez les anciennes affectations directes de `LocalTimeView` par `{present: true, time: value}`. Ne lisez `.time` que si `.present` vaut true. en.summary: Native text input for a local time of day.
en.usage: `accepted-time: LocalTimeValue` is an in-out typed value. `{}` or `{present: false}` means absence; `{present: true, time: {}}` is midnight. Replace former bare `LocalTimeView` assignments with `{present: true, time: value}`. Read `.time` only when `.present` is true. A local commit writes the parsed typed value back to this property (use a two-way `<=>` binding to share it); Controlled ownership leaves it for the host to acknowledge. Local/Controlled ownership also governs the shared FieldState and `committed(FieldCommit)`. Guard Rust acceptance with the matching FieldSpec and retain its parsed result. Import the component from `@kit`, set its labels and constraints, then call `slint_kit::install(&app)` once before showing the window. The field owns its native `text` draft and accepted value. For a domain codec, register a named `FieldSpec<T, E>` with `install_field_specs`, set `spec-key` and receive `committed(FieldCommit)`; `spec.accept(commit)` returns the validated domain value to Rust. `commit-policy` chooses blur, submit or each valid change. `ownership: Ownership.controlled` emits proposals and waits for `acknowledge(FieldValue)`. `field-state` and `accepted-text` expose the shared state; the native draft stays editable while incomplete. See the Forms guide for shared constraints and the Controllers guide for codecs. The typed time must fit `precision`; minute precision rejects a nonzero second instead of truncating it. `clock-format` controls 12/24-hour formatting.
en.behavior: After `slint_kit::install(&window)`, a valid typed host snapshot initializes the accepted baseline and formats idle text, including fields mounted after installation. Later host updates and explicit absence refresh idle text and baseline. An explicitly authored initial draft, even empty, is preserved. While the native editor has focus, host updates acknowledge the baseline without replacing its text, caret, selection or undo; reconciliation occurs at blur/cancel. Invalid typed models are ignored and never treated as absence. Pure-Slint previews need authored text; typed synchronization requires installed Rust services. Headless evidence does not qualify native IME or screen readers. LocalTime has no date or time zone. The visible label does not change the explicit clock-format. Pure-Slint previews display authored text; typed formatting, parsing and acceptance need the Rust services installed with `install(&window)`. See the editor guide for static preview limitations. ArrowUp/ArrowDown step the finest displayed unit (minutes, or seconds with `precision: TimePrecision.second`) and Page Up/Page Down step hours, within `min`, `max` and `step`. A draft that is not a time stays with the native editor.

fr.summary: Chronologie verticale de titres, descriptions et métadonnées.
fr.usage: Fournissez des `TimelineEntry` dans l’ordre souhaité, avec des métadonnées déjà formatées par le contrôleur. Prévoyez la hauteur nécessaire au texte agrandi ou placez la chronologie dans une zone de défilement.
fr.behavior: Chaque entrée est reliée par un marqueur et un trait visuels. La vue ne trie pas les événements et ne virtualise pas la collection. Chaque TimelineEntry accepte tone et un glyphe décoratif facultatif ; un glyphe vide conserve le repère circulaire. Le ton par défaut est neutre. Portez le sens dans title/description pour ne pas dépendre de la couleur ni de l’icône décorative.

en.summary: Vertical timeline of headings, descriptions and metadata.
en.usage: Supply `TimelineEntry` values in the desired order, with metadata already formatted by the controller. Allow height for enlarged text or place the timeline in a scroll area.
en.behavior: Each entry is connected by a visual marker and rule. The view neither sorts events nor virtualizes the collection. Each TimelineEntry accepts tone and an optional decorative glyph; empty glyphs keep the circular marker. Neutral is the default tone. Put the event meaning in title/description so status does not depend on color or the decorative icon.

fr.summary: Saisie d’heure locale avec réglage des heures et minutes.
fr.usage: `accepted-time` est un `LocalTimeValue` en entrée-sortie : `{}` signifie absence et `{present: true, time: {}}` signifie minuit. La propriété locale actualise ce modèle typé et émet `chosen(LocalTimeView)` pour une valeur présente ou `cleared()` pour une absence facultative valide. La propriété contrôlée propose les mêmes événements sans remplacer le modèle ; acquittez par l’affectation complète `{present: true, time: value}` ou `{present: false}`. `committed(FieldCommit)` reste disponible pour la frontière Rust FieldSpec partagée. Migrez toute ancienne affectation directe de LocalTimeView vers ce conteneur de présence.  Choisissez précision et format d’horloge, enregistrez un `FieldSpec` d’heure et traitez `committed(FieldCommit)`. Le kit ajuste les segments et le format ; `commit()` et `cancel-edit()` conservent le contrat partagé des champs. Les anciens callbacks d’ajustement restent des ports d’observation. L’heure typée doit respecter `precision` ; la précision à la minute refuse une seconde non nulle au lieu de la tronquer. `clock-format` gouverne le formatage sur 12/24 heures.
fr.behavior: Après `slint_kit::install(&window)`, un instantané hôte typé valide initialise la valeur acceptée de référence et formate le texte au repos, y compris pour un champ monté après installation. Les mises à jour hôte et l’absence explicite actualisent ensuite texte au repos et référence. Un brouillon initial explicitement défini, même vide, est conservé. Pendant le focus de l’éditeur natif, les mises à jour hôte acquittent la référence sans remplacer texte, curseur, sélection ni historique d’annulation ; la réconciliation intervient à la perte de focus ou à l’annulation. Les modèles typés invalides sont ignorés et ne représentent jamais une absence. La prévisualisation Slint seule nécessite un texte explicite ; la synchronisation typée exige les services Rust installés. Les preuves headless ne qualifient ni IME natif ni lecteur d’écran. Un brouillon vide prend la première heure légale exactement représentable à la précision choisie, à partir de min valide, sinon de la valeur par défaut valide des contraintes partagées lorsqu’elle est fournie, sinon de minuit/du premier point permis. Le premier clic choisit cette valeur sans ajouter un pas ; incrément et décrément utilisent le même départ. TimePicker `default-value` est l’heure que `reset-field()` rétablit, et la valeur de départ en l’absence de `min`. Un brouillon non vide invalide/incomplet reste inchangé. Les déplacements utilisent l’intersection de la grille exacte du pas et des minutes/secondes entières imposées par precision ; aucune heure n’est arrondie. Chaque bouton déplace ceil(durée du segment / pas représentable) pas de grille ; avec step: "900", minute/seconde déplace de 15 minutes et heure d’une heure. Une valeur hors grille retrouve une valeur dans le sens demandé. L’arithmétique propage les retenues entre segments (10:59 → 11:00) sans changer de date. Sans bornes valides, elle boucle sur 24 heures sur la grille ; des bornes ordinaires limitent le déplacement aux extrémités légales. min > max décrit un intervalle périodique traversant minuit (23:00–02:00) : le déplacement peut passer minuit dans cet intervalle, puis se limite à ses extrémités. step est exprimé en secondes ; any supprime la contrainte de grille, un pas mal formé/non positif prend le défaut HTML time de 60 secondes, et les bornes mal formées sont ignorées. Sans candidat légal représentable, aucune modification ni acceptation. replace-draft natif conserve l’éditeur monté et l’historique/les notifications d’édition avant validation partagée du commit. Désactivation/lecture seule, préédition native active et services indisponibles bloquent le remplacement. Publication/acquittement Local/Controlled conservent leur contrat typé ; adjust est une observation, pas une donnée acceptée. Maintenir un bouton Heures/Minutes/Secondes répète l’ajustement après 400 ms, toutes les 80 ms ; le relâchement n’ajoute aucun pas et la répétition s’arrête quand la borne ou la grille n’admet plus de déplacement. Chaque ligne de segment est aussi un bouton rotatif (accessible-role spinbox) nommé comme la ligne, avec le texte du segment comme valeur (vide tant que le brouillon est vide ou incomplet), le minimum/maximum du segment (heures 0-23, ou 1-12 en horloge 12 heures ; minutes et secondes 0-59), le pas dans cette unité et des actions incrément/décrément partagées avec les boutons, qui respectent désactivé/lecture seule. Les boutons visuels +/- restent des boutons en dessous. Les preuves headless ne qualifient pas les lecteurs d’écran ; aucune refonte en éditeur segmenté n’est fournie. Les aperçus Slint seuls affichent le texte déclaré ; formatage typé, analyse et acceptation nécessitent les services Rust installés par `install(&window)`. Le guide de l’éditeur détaille les limites des aperçus.
fr.label: Sélecteur d’heure

functions.report-validity: Signale les erreurs de contrainte et retourne la validité en conservant le focus. Le formulaire peut recueillir tous les résultats avant de déplacer une seule fois le focus.
functions.focus-if-invalid: Demande le focus normal de l’éditeur ou du contrôle uniquement si ce candidat à la validation est invalide ; retourne si le focus a été demandé. Cette fonction ne signale pas les erreurs de nouveau.

modal-layer.effect: La couche modale à laquelle appartient ce composant ; 0 est la fenêtre. Tant qu’un `KitDialogSurface` ou `KitDrawer` dont `modal-layer` est positif est ouvert et au sommet, le composant est inerte : son champ et ses boutons de réglage ne prennent pas le focus et ignorent le pointeur et les touches. Donnez à un composant placé dans une modale le numéro de couche de cette modale.

accepted-time.effect: Instantané hôte de type `LocalTimeValue`. `accepted-time` est un `LocalTimeValue` en entrée-sortie : `{}` signifie absence et `{present: true, time: {}}` signifie minuit. La propriété locale actualise ce modèle typé et émet `chosen(LocalTimeView)` pour une valeur présente ou `cleared()` pour une absence facultative valide. La propriété contrôlée propose les mêmes événements sans remplacer le modèle ; acquittez par l’affectation complète `{present: true, time: value}` ou `{present: false}`. `committed(FieldCommit)` reste disponible pour la frontière Rust FieldSpec partagée. Migrez toute ancienne affectation directe de LocalTimeView vers ce conteneur de présence.

step.effect: Secondes entre valeurs admissibles. Le déplacement croise cette grille exacte avec la précision choisie ; 900 signifie 15 minutes. any retire la contrainte de grille ; un pas mal formé/non positif prend le défaut HTML time de 60 secondes.
step.default: 60 en précision minute ; 1 en précision seconde.

min.effect: Borne basse inclusive au format horaire canonique et base du pas si valide ; avec min > max, la plage permise traverse minuit. Les bornes mal formées sont ignorées.

max.effect: Borne haute inclusive au format horaire canonique ; avec min > max, elle termine après minuit une plage périodique. Les bornes mal formées sont ignorées.

required-message.effect: Message affiché quand `required` est actif et que la valeur est vide. Remplace la valeur par défaut de la fenêtre pour cette instance.

underflow-message.effect: Message affiché quand la valeur est inférieure à `min`. Le modèle par défaut est `KitStrings.underflow-template`, où `{value}` est remplacé par `min`. Remplace la valeur par défaut de la fenêtre pour cette instance.

overflow-message.effect: Message affiché quand la valeur dépasse `max`. Le modèle par défaut est `KitStrings.overflow-template`, où `{value}` est remplacé par `max`. Remplace la valeur par défaut de la fenêtre pour cette instance.

step-message.effect: Message affiché quand la valeur n’est pas sur la grille de `step`. Remplace la valeur par défaut de la fenêtre pour cette instance.

bad-input-message.effect: Message affiché quand le texte n’est pas une valeur valide de ce champ. Remplace la valeur par défaut de la fenêtre pour cette instance.

hours-label.effect: Nom du segment, annoncé par les technologies d’assistance et affiché à côté de ses boutons.

minutes-label.effect: Nom du segment, annoncé par les technologies d’assistance et affiché à côté de ses boutons.

seconds-label.effect: Nom du segment, annoncé par les technologies d’assistance et affiché à côté de ses boutons.

increase-template.effect: Nom accessible de chaque bouton d’augmentation. `{label}` représente le libellé du segment : chaque langue choisit son ordre des mots.

decrease-template.effect: Nom accessible de chaque bouton de diminution. `{label}` représente le libellé du segment.

placeholder.effect: Indication affichée dans l’éditeur d’heure vide. C’est un indice de format : adaptez-le au méridien que votre application accepte.

description.effect: Texte d’aide de l’éditeur d’heure, lu par les technologies d’assistance.

callbacks.chosen: `chosen(LocalTimeView)` : heure locale présente validée. Local actualise accepted-time ; Controlled attend l’acquittement hôte.
callbacks.cleared: Absence facultative valide acceptée ; acquittez avec accepted-time: {present: false} en mode Controlled. Il s’agit d’une acceptation, pas d’une observation d’effacement du brouillon.
callbacks.committed: `committed(FieldCommit)` : validation partagée conservée pour l’acceptation Rust typée.
callbacks.adjust: `adjust(TimeSegment, TimeAdjustment)` observe une demande de déplacement. Il ne prouve ni modification du brouillon ni acceptation ; consommez chosen/cleared ou validez committed avec FieldSpec.

en.summary: Local-time input with hour and minute adjustment controls.
en.usage: `accepted-time` is an in-out `LocalTimeValue`: `{}` means absence and `{present: true, time: {}}` means midnight. Local ownership updates this typed model and emits `chosen(LocalTimeView)` for a present value or `cleared()` for valid optional absence. Controlled ownership proposes the same events without replacing the model; acknowledge with the complete `{present: true, time: value}` or `{present: false}` assignment. `committed(FieldCommit)` remains available for the shared Rust FieldSpec boundary. Migrate every former bare LocalTimeView assignment to the presence wrapper.  Choose precision and clock format, register a time `FieldSpec`, and handle `committed(FieldCommit)`. Segment adjustment and formatting run in the kit; `commit()` and `cancel-edit()` preserve the shared field contract. Legacy adjustment callbacks remain observation ports. The typed time must fit `precision`; minute precision rejects a nonzero second instead of truncating it. `clock-format` controls 12/24-hour formatting.
en.behavior: After `slint_kit::install(&window)`, a valid typed host snapshot initializes the accepted baseline and formats idle text, including fields mounted after installation. Later host updates and explicit absence refresh idle text and baseline. An explicitly authored initial draft, even empty, is preserved. While the native editor has focus, host updates acknowledge the baseline without replacing its text, caret, selection or undo; reconciliation occurs at blur/cancel. Invalid typed models are ignored and never treated as absence. Pure-Slint previews need authored text; typed synchronization requires installed Rust services. Headless evidence does not qualify native IME or screen readers. An empty draft seeds the first legal time exactly representable at the selected precision, starting from a valid min, otherwise the shared constraints’ valid default value when supplied, otherwise midnight/the first permitted point. The first click selects that seed without adding another step; increment and decrement use the same seed. TimePicker `default-value` is the time `reset-field()` restores, and the seed when `min` is absent. Nonempty invalid/incomplete drafts remain unchanged. Adjustments use the intersection of the exact step lattice and whole minutes/seconds required by precision; no time value is rounded. Each button moves ceil(segment duration / representable step) lattice steps; with step: "900", minute/second adjustment moves 15 minutes and hour adjustment moves one hour. Off-grid values recover in the requested direction. Arithmetic carries across segments (10:59 → 11:00) without changing a date. Without valid bounds it wraps over 24 hours on the lattice; ordinary bounds clamp at legal endpoints. min > max describes a periodic interval across midnight (23:00–02:00): movement may cross midnight inside that interval, then clamps at its endpoints. step is in seconds; any removes the step-grid restriction, malformed/nonpositive step uses the HTML time default of 60 seconds, and malformed bounds are ignored. No representable legal candidate means no edit or acceptance. Native replace-draft preserves the mounted editor and undo/edit notifications before shared commit validation. Disabled/read-only, active native preedit and unavailable services block replacement. Local/Controlled publication and acknowledgement keep their existing typed contract; adjust is an observation, not accepted data. Holding a Hours/Minutes/Seconds button repeats its adjustment after 400 ms every 80 ms; the release adds no extra step and repetition stops when the bound or lattice admits no further move. Each segment row is also a spin button (accessible-role spinbox) named like the row, with the segment text as value (empty while the draft is empty or incomplete), the segment minimum/maximum (hours 0-23, or 1-12 with a 12-hour clock; minutes and seconds 0-59), the step in that unit and increment/decrement actions that share the button path and respect disabled/read-only. The visual +/- buttons stay available as buttons below it. Headless coverage does not qualify screen readers, and a segmented-editor redesign is not provided. Pure-Slint previews display authored text; typed formatting, parsing and acceptance need the Rust services installed with `install(&window)`. See the editor guide for static preview limitations.
en.label: Time Picker

functions.report-validity: Report constraint failures and return validity while preserving the current focus. Form coordinators can collect every result before moving focus once.
functions.focus-if-invalid: Request the normal editor/control focus only when this enabled validation candidate is invalid; return whether focus was requested. This function does not report errors again.

modal-layer.effect: The modal layer this component belongs to; 0 is the window. While a `KitDialogSurface` or `KitDrawer` with a positive `modal-layer` is open and topmost, the component is inert: its field and spin buttons take no focus and ignore pointer and keys. Give a component placed inside a modal that modal’s layer number.

accepted-time.effect: Host snapshot of type `LocalTimeValue`. `accepted-time` is an in-out `LocalTimeValue`: `{}` means absence and `{present: true, time: {}}` means midnight. Local ownership updates this typed model and emits `chosen(LocalTimeView)` for a present value or `cleared()` for valid optional absence. Controlled ownership proposes the same events without replacing the model; acknowledge with the complete `{present: true, time: value}` or `{present: false}` assignment. `committed(FieldCommit)` remains available for the shared Rust FieldSpec boundary. Migrate every former bare LocalTimeView assignment to the presence wrapper.

step.effect: Seconds between admissible values. Adjustment intersects this exact grid with the selected precision; 900 means 15 minutes. any removes the grid restriction; malformed/nonpositive values fall back to HTML time’s 60 seconds.
step.default: 60 for minute precision; 1 for second precision.

min.effect: Inclusive canonical time lower endpoint and step base when valid; with min > max the permitted range crosses midnight. Malformed bounds are ignored.

max.effect: Inclusive canonical time upper endpoint; with min > max this is the end after midnight of a periodic range. Malformed bounds are ignored.

required-message.effect: Message shown when `required` is set and the value is empty. Overrides the window default for this instance.

underflow-message.effect: Message shown when the value is below `min`. Replace `{value}` in your template with the bound; the default is `KitStrings.underflow-template` with `{value}` replaced by `min`. Overrides the window default for this instance.

overflow-message.effect: Message shown when the value is above `max`. The default is `KitStrings.overflow-template` with `{value}` replaced by `max`. Overrides the window default for this instance.

step-message.effect: Message shown when the value is off the `step` grid. Overrides the window default for this instance.

bad-input-message.effect: Message shown when the text is not a valid value of this field. Overrides the window default for this instance.

hours-label.effect: Name of the hours spin button, announced by assistive technology and shown beside it.

minutes-label.effect: Name of the minutes spin button, announced by assistive technology and shown beside it.

seconds-label.effect: Name of the seconds spin button, announced by assistive technology and shown beside it.

increase-template.effect: Accessible name of each increase button. `{label}` stands for the segment label, so each language chooses its word order.

decrease-template.effect: Accessible name of each decrease button. `{label}` stands for the segment label.

placeholder.effect: Hint shown in the empty time editor. It is a format hint, so translate it with the meridiem your application accepts.

description.effect: Help text of the time editor, read by assistive technology.

callbacks.chosen: `chosen(LocalTimeView)`: validated present local time. Local updates accepted-time; Controlled waits for host acknowledgement.
callbacks.cleared: Committed valid optional absence; acknowledge with accepted-time: {present: false} in Controlled mode. This is acceptance, not a draft-clear observation.
callbacks.committed: `committed(FieldCommit)`: preserved shared field commit for typed Rust acceptance.
callbacks.adjust: `adjust(TimeSegment, TimeAdjustment)` observes an adjustment request. It does not prove that the draft changed or a value was accepted; consume chosen/cleared or validate committed through FieldSpec.

fr.summary: Notification transitoire identifiable avec action et fermeture facultatives.
fr.usage: Utilisez `ToastBinding<Action>` avec des actions métier typées, une capacité et `ToastLifetime`. Fournissez `model()` à l’hôte ou répétez `KitToast`. Connectez `action_handler`, `dismiss_handler` et `interaction_handler` ; expiration et pauses indépendantes du pointeur et du focus restent dans le kit. Le minuteur ne retient ni fenêtre ni son propre état. Conservez le ToastId renvoyé par push côté Rust. Enregistrez on_closed(id, action, reason) pour observer Expired, Dismissed, Action, Evicted et Cleared ; un nouvel enregistrement remplace le précédent. dismiss_id(id), clear(), len()/is_empty() et update(id, view, lifetime) appartiennent à ToastBinding, sans nouvelle propriété ni callback Slint. T reste Clone ; l’observateur reçoit un clone de l’action tandis que la fermeture peut la retourner.
fr.behavior: `ToastInteraction.pointer` et `.focus` sont deux sources de pause distinctes. La vue n’ajoute pas de minuterie ; le contrôleur conserve le temps restant et les identités stables. Les notifications de fermeture Rust suivent la publication du modèle/minuteur sans emprunt du binding retenu : les mutations réentrantes sont conservées. action_handler signale Action avant le métier, une fois. update conserve ID/jeton, action typée et pauses indépendantes, redémarre la durée à maintenant et ne ferme pas une simple mise à jour ; un ID absent/expiré renvoie false sans résurrection. Persistent empêche l’expiration, pas l’éviction de capacité ni la fermeture explicite. La file retourne les expirations avant l’éviction avec les charges utiles entières. Les observateurs UI doivent capturer une fenêtre faible ; le minuteur ne retient toujours aucune fenêtre.
fr.label: Notification toast

dismiss-label.effect: Nom accessible complet de fermeture. Utilise entry.dismiss-label si non vide, sinon remplace le titre dans le modèle global.

entry.effect: ToastEntry porte dismiss-label pour un nom complet par entrée ; une chaîne vide utilise le modèle global Dismiss {title}.
entry.constraints: Les littéraux Rust complets doivent inclure dismiss_label ; ..Default::default() reste compatible.

fr.accessibility: Chaque toast dessine une marque de sévérité (coche, signal d’avertissement ou information) teintée par la recette d’alerte : la sévérité ne repose plus sur la seule couleur du titre. Échap sur le bouton d’action ou de fermeture ayant le focus ferme un toast fermable, comme sur un toast web ; un toast sans fermeture l’ignore. Localisez le nom accessible de l’action ou de la région avec les propriétés documentées ou les défauts KitStrings de la fenêtre. La qualification d’un lecteur d’écran reste propre au backend et à l’appareil.

functions.take-focus: Place le focus clavier sur l’action du toast, ou sur son bouton de fermeture s’il n’a pas d’action. Sans effet pour un toast sans ces deux contrôles.

en.summary: Identified transient notification with optional action and dismissal.
en.usage: Use `ToastBinding<Action>` with typed business actions, queue capacity and `ToastLifetime`. Pass `model()` to the host or repeat `KitToast` over it. Connect `action_handler`, `dismiss_handler` and `interaction_handler`; expiry and independent pointer/focus pauses stay in the kit. The timer retains neither a window nor its own state. Retain the ToastId returned by Rust push. Register on_closed(id, action, reason) to observe Expired, Dismissed, Action, Evicted and Cleared; registering again replaces the previous handler. dismiss_id(id), clear(), len()/is_empty() and update(id, view, lifetime) belong to ToastBinding, not Slint properties or callbacks. T remains Clone; the close observer receives an action clone while dismissal can return the action.
en.behavior: `ToastInteraction.pointer` and `.focus` are separate pause sources. The view adds no timer; the controller preserves remaining lifetime and stable identities. Rust closure notifications run after model/timer publication without a held binding borrow, so reentrant mutations survive. action_handler reports Action closure before invoking business code, once. update preserves ID/token, typed action and independent pauses, restarts the duration at now and emits no close event for a simple update; a missing/expired ID returns false without resurrection. Persistent suppresses timeout, not capacity eviction or explicit closure. The queue reports expired records before capacity eviction, with full payloads. UI observers must capture a weak window; the timer still retains no window.

dismiss-label.effect: Complete accessible dismiss-action name. Defaults to entry.dismiss-label when nonempty; otherwise substitutes the entry title into the global template.

entry.effect: ToastEntry carries dismiss-label for a complete per-entry name; an empty string uses the global Dismiss {title} template.
entry.constraints: Complete Rust literals must include dismiss_label; ..Default::default() remains compatible.

en.accessibility: Each toast draws a severity mark (check, warning sign or information) tinted by the alert recipe, so severity never rests on the title color alone. Escape on the focused action or dismiss button closes a dismissible toast, like Escape on a web toast; a toast without dismissal ignores it. Localize the accessible action/region name through the documented properties or per-window KitStrings defaults. Screen-reader qualification remains backend/device-specific.

functions.take-focus: Move keyboard focus to the toast action, or to its dismiss button when there is no action. Does nothing for a toast with neither control.

fr.usage: Utilisez `ToastBinding<Action>` avec des actions métier typées, une capacité et `ToastLifetime`. Fournissez `model()` à l’hôte ou répétez `KitToast`. Connectez `action_handler`, `dismiss_handler` et `interaction_handler` ; expiration et pauses indépendantes du pointeur et du focus restent dans le kit. Le minuteur ne retient ni fenêtre ni son propre état. Conservez le ToastId renvoyé par push côté Rust. fr.behavior: Chaque entrée est rendue par `KitToast` sans minuterie par délégué. Le propriétaire décide des durées, de l’ordre et des suppressions en conservant le temps restant après une pause. Les entrées conservées gardent leurs boutons montés, le focus clavier et leurs pauses indépendantes de survol/focus lorsqu’un autre toast est ajouté, fermé, expire ou est évincé ; gardez le même modèle ToastBinding installé. ToastBinding côté Rust arme un minuteur unique pour la prochaine durée active et l’arrête si la file est vide, entièrement persistante ou entièrement en pause. Les pauses pointeur et focus conservent leur durée restante indépendante ; les changements de file préservent les identités des délégués conservés. Les notifications de fermeture Rust suivent la publication du modèle/minuteur sans emprunt du binding retenu : les mutations réentrantes sont conservées. action_handler signale Action avant le métier, une fois. update conserve ID/jeton, action typée et pauses indépendantes, redémarre la durée à maintenant et ne ferme pas une simple mise à jour ; un ID absent/expiré renvoie false sans résurrection. Persistent empêche l’expiration, pas l’éviction de capacité ni la fermeture explicite. La file retourne les expirations avant l’éviction avec les charges utiles entières. Les observateurs UI doivent capturer une fenêtre faible ; le minuteur ne retient toujours aucune fenêtre.
fr.label: Pile de notifications toast
fr.seoTitle: Pile de notifications toast pour Slint

entries.effect: Chaque ToastEntry peut fournir dismiss-label ; l’hôte le transmet à son KitToast. Un libellé vide utilise KitStrings.dismiss-label-template avec le titre de l’entrée.
